findings.quote: it names something the text really does spend room on
findings.note: class 3 (idiom/collocation): “spend room on” is not an English collocation — a blend of “have room for” and “spend time/space on”. Newly rewritten Q1/C rationale text. Editor's rewrite: 'it names something the text really does give room to'.

findings.quote: only one of the readings it allows is the forecast’s fault; the rest are the camera’s
findings.note: class 3 (idiom): new ¶5 prose. A *reading* cannot be a fault — the fault belongs to the cause, not to the interpretation; the sentence silently swaps the two. Editor's rewrite: 'only one of the readings it allows blames the forecast; the rest blame the camera.'

findings.quote: the forecast’s own author points the same way
findings.note: class 3 (collocation): new ¶5 prose. 'point the same way' collocates with evidence, indicators or findings, not with a person. Editor's rewrite: 'and the forecast's own author says as much'.

findings.quote: so a large share of them were made into air that would have produced nothing anyway
findings.note: class 3 (collocation/garden path): 'made into' reads as 'transformed into' before the reader recovers 'flown into'. Editor's rewrite: 'so a large share of them took airplanes down into air that would have produced nothing anyway'.

findings.quote: The layer has “nothing in it to look at” and makes “no cloud of its own”, because
findings.note: class 4 (house style / declared-variety consistency): the passage sets terminal commas and periods INSIDE the closing quote (AmE, 4/4); the rationale layer sets them OUTSIDE (BrE 'logical' style, 10 of 11 instances). The unit declares spelling_variety AmE. Pick one — AmE, to match the passage.

findings.quote: it names something the text really does spend room on
findings.note: class 3 (collocation): 'spend room on' has no native currency; it is 'have room for' crossed with 'spend space/time on'. Editor's rewrite: 'really does spend space on' or 'really does dwell on'.

findings.quote: The reader supplies the join and re-describes the held-in heat as the warming
findings.note: class 1/3 (variety drift): the noun 'join' in the sense of seam/junction is labelled chiefly British; an AmE-declared unit wants 'the connection' or 'the link'. The same sentence then reaches for the gerund ('no second joining'), so the noun is not even carrying its own weight. Editor's rewrite: 'The reader supplies the connection'.

findings.quote: “pull against one another” says that the two oppose, not which of them wins
findings.note: class 2/3 (valency): modern English 'oppose' is transitive; bare intransitive 'the two oppose' is nonstandard and an editor would strike it. Editor's rewrite: 'says that the two are opposed, not which of them wins'.

findings.quote: cannot be answered with a thing the text conspicuously leaves open
findings.note: class 3/4 (idiom/register): 'with a thing' for 'with something' is thin and reads ESL-flavoured in otherwise controlled expository prose. Editor's rewrite: 'cannot be answered with something the text conspicuously leaves open'.

findings.quote: the only depth given is the small hill, and it is not time-of-day dependent
findings.note: class 4 (house style): unhyphenated compound modifier. Editor's rewrite: 'and it does not depend on the time of day'.

findings.quote: He calls the satellite count “the smallest thing those two winters produced”,
findings.note: class 4 (declared-variety consistency): comma outside the closing quote (BrE logical style) while the passage itself punctuates inside the quote (AmE). 10 of 11 rationale instances go BrE, 1 goes AmE, and the unit declares AmE. Normalize to AmE.

findings.quote: it names something the text really does spend room on
findings.note: class 3 (collocation): 'spend room on' is not idiomatic English. Editor's rewrite: 'that the text really does give room to'.

findings.quote: WHY-KEY (C): 141 airplanes were sent through air the forecast had called wet
findings.note: class 4 (house style): sentence opens on a numeral, which magazine style forbids. Editor's rewrite: 'Some 141 airplanes were sent through air the forecast had called wet'.

findings.quote: and the word cool is never used of a contrail
findings.note: class 4 (house style, use vs mention): the word-as-word is unmarked here and in 'Worthless is a word for evidence that says nothing either way', while the same rationales correctly quote “Also” and “pull against one another”. Editor's rewrite: 'and the word “cool” is never used of a contrail'.

findings.quote: many of the descents rather than all of them, and will have bought nothing rather than bought nothing
findings.note: class 4 (typography/clarity): four unmarked mentions in one clause; without quotation marks the contrast is unreadable on first pass. Editor's rewrite: '“many of the descents” rather than “all of them”, and “will have bought nothing” rather than “bought nothing”'.

findings.quote: where he names among the findings that will outlast the trial “that the forecast asks for more descents than the sky calls for”
findings.note: class 2/4 (syntax): 'name' takes a nominal, not a bare that-clause, and the adjunct is wedged between verb and object. Editor's rewrite: 'where he lists, among the findings that will outlast the trial, the fact that the forecast asks for more descents than the sky calls for'.

findings.quote: a forecast asking for more than the sky supplies is the best of those readings
findings.note: class 3 (category slip in paraphrase): a forecast is not a reading. The passage fronts a that-clause ('That the forecast asks for more than the sky supplies is the best of those readings'); the rationale's nominalization loses that and predicates 'reading' of the forecast itself. Editor's rewrite: 'that the forecast asks for more than the sky supplies is the best of those readings'.

findings.quote: and believes the rest would follow. Perhaps it would.
findings.note: class 2 (pronoun number): 'them' (the hundred sensors) governs the sentence, so 'the rest' reads as a countable plural and the echo wants 'Perhaps they would.' Defensible only if 'the rest' is read as a singular remainder. Editor's rewrite: 'Perhaps they would.'

findings.quote: paragraphs 3 to 5, the trial, the audit and the counting, do not touch crystal growth at all
findings.note: class 4 (house style): no serial comma here, but the same rationale uses one two sentences earlier ('cannot see a young contrail, cannot see its height, and cannot tell four or five tracks apart'). Pick one convention.
